::: {.content-visible when-format="docx"}
# Book_09 — The Transformed Posture: Continuous Governance and the 2027 Milestone
:::

::: {.callout-note}
A transformation that achieves a completed state and then stops monitoring is a transformation that will regress. The transformed posture is not a permanent state achieved by a one-time action — it is an ongoing condition maintained by continuous monitoring, automated drift detection, and a governance process that treats regression as a compliance violation. (ADR-068 Phase C, UIAO_135 Transformation #7)
:::

![After: the claims the OAuth 2.0 token carries — identity claims (upn, oid, groups, exp) and context claims (amr, acr, deviceid, compliant, ipaddr) — and why each matters to SQL Server.](images/card-after-02-token.svg){#fig-book-09-card-after-02 fig-alt="Card diagram on white background. Title: AFTER — Application-Aware Token (2 of 3: What the Token Carries). Left panel: OAuth 2.0 token anatomy with Identity and Context sections listing all claims. ![The OAuth 2.0 token session lifecycle — UML sequence diagram tracing auth+MFA through Conditional Access evaluation, token issuance, SQL validation, and silent token refresh.](images/seq-token-lifecycle.svg){#fig-book-09-seq-token fig-alt="UML sequence diagram on white background. Seven numbered steps: auth+MFA, CA evaluation, policy result with CA checks badge, signed token, token presented, SQL validation box, connection open. Silent refresh step shown dashed. Footer: token expiry 60-75 min, no domain controller at any step." width="100%"}
